competitors.name: Opticabase (with Opticabase Home add-on)
competitors.what_they_offer: UK optical practice management system (recalls, dispensing, clinical notes, eGOS England) with an 'Opticabase Home' add-on described as 'Software for Optician domiciliary providers without the need for an internet connnection'. A 2022 AOP feature says it also provides an electronic solution for pre-visit notifications and that over 650 practices in the UK and Ireland use Opticabase.
competitors.pricing: Published ex VAT: Full Clinical System £195/month/practice; Opticabase Home add-on £70/month/practice (£35/month for fewer than 35 domiciliary visits/month); SMS 5.5p per text
competitors.overlap: Domiciliary eye care focus; offline working on visits; patient records; SMS messaging; pre-visit notification handling (per AOP 2022)
competitors.gap_vs_domi: Waiting-list refill of cancelled slots by text, cancel-by-text reply, route planning/least-driving booking and online referral form are not mentioned on the pages fetched. Note: Opticabase appears to be ahead of Domi on eGOS/PVN, which Domi still lodges by hand.

competitors.name: Blink OMS (GenerationNET)
competitors.what_they_offer: Cloud-based optician management system with integrated eGOS submission to PCSE, online booking through the practice website, recalls and SMS text reminders to patients in the next clinic.
competitors.overlap: Cloud diary accessible remotely; SMS reminders; online booking; patient records
competitors.gap_vs_domi: Domiciliary services, waiting-list refill, route planning, offline clinician app and referral intake are not mentioned on their site. (Search snippets claim domiciliary use and £30–£145/month pricing, but these were not confirmed on a fetched page.)

competitors.name: Acuitas 3 (Ocuco)
competitors.what_they_offer: Optical practice management software for UK practices covering scheduling, staff and clinic performance, eGOS integration (GOS1, GOS3, GOS4), and recall/marketing with automatic recalls, SMS reminders and email marketing.
competitors.overlap: Appointment diary; SMS appointment confirmations and recalls; online booking (mentioned in a testimonial)
competitors.gap_vs_domi: Domiciliary/home visits, waiting lists, route planning and referral forms are not mentioned on the page fetched; appears clinic/high-street oriented.

competitors.name: OctopusPro (Mobile Optometrist & Domiciliary Optician Scheduling)
competitors.what_they_offer: Generic field-service platform with a page marketed at mobile optometrists and domiciliary opticians: practitioner rotas and visit routes on one calendar, proximity-based scheduling, GPS tracking, branded online booking portal, automated email/SMS/app reminders and a practitioner mobile app with forms that 'can be completed online or offline'.
competitors.pricing: Published: Starter $36.25/month ($348/year); Established $60 USD per admin seat + $6 USD per fieldworker seat per month; Unlimited Users $99 USD platform fee/month plus $1 per booked job or 2% of invoiced revenue
competitors.overlap: Home-visit scheduling; route planning & optimisation (listed on all plans); SMS reminders and two-way SMS; online booking; clinician mobile app with offline forms
competitors.gap_vs_domi: Waiting-list refill of cancelled slots is not mentioned; no NHS/GOS, PVN or eye-care clinical records (prescription, glasses) mentioned; priced in USD and not UK-specific; referral intake not mentioned.

competitors.name: OptimoRoute
competitors.what_they_offer: Route optimisation and planning tool with automated planning, weekly planning (Pro), a driver mobile app that receives routes and sends real-time updates, and real-time order tracking with customer ETA notifications.
competitors.pricing: Published per driver per month, billed annually: Lite $35.10; Pro $44.10; Custom on request
competitors.overlap: Route planning/optimisation of a day's visits; field app; customer ETA notifications (similar to 'On my way' text)
competitors.gap_vs_domi: Not healthcare-specific: no patient records, waiting list, cancellation refill, referrals or GDPR subject-access tools mentioned; SMS not explicitly mentioned on the pricing page.

competitors.name: Cal.com
competitors.what_they_offer: General booking/scheduling tool with an optometry page offering routing/intake forms that match patients to the right optometrist, calendar sync with Google/Outlook/Apple, multi-location bookings, analytics and a self-hosting option.
competitors.overlap: Online booking and intake forms (loosely comparable to Domi's referral form)
competitors.gap_vs_domi: Reminders, SMS, waitlists and home visits are not mentioned on the page fetched; no route planning or clinical records mentioned.

positioning_takeaways: None of the six fetched competitor pages mention automatically refilling a cancelled slot from a waiting list by text, so 'acts on the gap' appears to be a genuine differentiator — re-verify each vendor before saying so publicly, and avoid absolute 'only' claims.

Optical PMS vendors (Opticabase, Blink OMS, Acuitas 3) lead on NHS eGOS integration and, for Opticabase, pre-visit notifications; Domi lodges PCSE notifications by hand, so messaging should position Domi on diary/refill/routing rather than NHS claims, or as complementary to an existing PMS.
Opticabase publishes a dedicated domiciliary add-on price (£70/month, or £35/month under 35 visits/month, on top of £195/month), giving a visible UK price anchor for domiciliary software buyers.

Generic field-service and routing tools (OctopusPro, OptimoRoute) cover route optimisation and SMS reminders but publish USD pricing and do not mention NHS/eye-care records; Domi can stress being built for UK domiciliary eye care with clinical context (prescriptions, alerts) in the clinician app.

Offline working is offered by Opticabase Home and OctopusPro forms, so offline support is table stakes rather than a differentiator; recovered-income reporting and least-driving booking are not mentioned by any fetched competitor and may resonate more.
